python -c "
import toolz
from collections import OrderedDict

# Test merge with OrderedDict
od = OrderedDict([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
merge_result = toolz.merge(od, {'c': 3})
print(f'merge(OrderedDict([(\"a\", 1)]), {{\"c\": 3}}) = {merge_result}')
print(f'Type: {type(merge_result)}')
assert isinstance(merge_result, OrderedDict), f'Expected OrderedDict, got {type(merge_result)}'

# Test merge_with with OrderedDict
merge_with_result = toolz.merge_with(sum, od, {'a': 10, 'd': 4})
print(f'merge_with_result = {merge_with_result}')
print(f'Type: {type(merge_with_result)}')
assert isinstance(merge_with_result, OrderedDict), f'Expected OrderedDict, got {type(merge_with_result)}'

# Test merge with regular dict still works
regular_merge = toolz.merge({'a': 1}, {'b': 2})
print(f'regular_merge = {regular_merge}')
assert isinstance(regular_merge, dict), f'Expected dict, got {type(regular_merge)}'

# Test merge with explicit factory still works
factory_merge = toolz.merge({'a': 1}, factory=OrderedDict)
print(f'factory_merge = {factory_merge}')
assert isinstance(factory_merge, OrderedDict), f'Expected OrderedDict, got {type(factory_merge)}'

print('All merge tests passed!')
"
